title: Baba in Wonderland: Online Self-Supervised Dynamics Discovery for Executable World Models
abstract: arXiv:2605.16725v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Executable world models can be read, edited, executed, and reused for planning, but only if the program captures the environment's transition law rather than semantic shortcuts in its surface vocabulary. We study online executable world-model learning under prior misalignment, where an agent must induce state-dependent dynamics from interaction evidence alone, without rule descriptions, reward signals, or trustworthy lexical priors. We introduce Alice, a closed-loop system that treats failed candidate updates as structural signal: when a candidate explains a new transition but loses previously explained ones, the preservation conflict reveals dynamics that the current program had conflated. translated_title: Baba漫游奇境：面向可执行世界模型的在线自监督动力学发现
translated_abstract: 可执行世界模型可以被读取、编辑、执行并复用于规划，但前提是程序捕获的是环境的转移规律，而非其表面词汇中的语义捷径。我们研究了先验失配情况下的在线可执行世界模型学习问题：此时智能体必须仅凭交互证据归纳出依赖于状态的动力学，无法依赖规则描述、奖励信号或可信的词汇先验。我们提出了Alice，一个闭环系统，它将失败的候选更新视为结构性信号：当一个候选能够解释新的转移却丢失了先前已解释的转移时，这种保持性冲突便揭示了当前程序所混淆的动力学。Alice将这些冲突细化为假设类，这些假设类一方面为更新提供少量被破坏的例子（每个受影响的类别各一个），另一方面引导前沿探索走向相对当前程序而言新颖且欠表示的转移。
tldr: 提出Alice闭环系统，将候选更新失败引发的“保持性冲突”作为结构性信号，归纳出假设类以修复可执行世界模型并引导前沿探索，从而仅凭交互证据实现先验失配下的在线自监督环境动力学发现。
en_tdlr: Alice is a closed-loop system that treats failed candidate updates—where explaining new transitions breaks previously explained ones—as structural signals, refining preservation conflicts into hypothesis classes to repair executable world models and guide frontier exploration toward novel, underrepresented dynamics.
